parts.model_answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\sin t}{1-\cos t}=1$ at $t=\frac{\pi}{2}$; the point is $\left(-3 + \frac{3 \pi}{2},3\right)$, so $y-3=x-(-3 + \frac{3 \pi}{2})$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Solves dy/dt = 0 on the interval and checks dx/dt is not 0

rubric_rows.criterion: Error bound is the first omitted term a_9 (value)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Let $R_N=\displaystyle\sum_{n=N+1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{n^2+4}$ be the remainder after the first $N$ terms of the series in part (a). ap_calculus_bc-f06.title: Taylor polynomial from a table of derivatives, an approximation, a Lagrange error bound, and the Second Derivative Test

stimulus.description: Values of f and its derivatives at the center

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A function $f$ has derivatives of all orders. The table gives the values of $f^{(k)}(2)$ for $k=0,1,2,3$, and $\left|f^{(4)}(x)\right|\le48$ for all $x$ in the interval $[2,3]$. Write the third-degree Taylor polynomial $P_3(x)$ for $f$ about $x=2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses f(a), f'(a), f''(a)/2!, f'''(a)/3! as the coefficients (setup)

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use $P_3$ to approximate $f\left(2+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.
parts.model_answer: $P_3\left(2+\frac12\right)=\frac{13}{4}$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use the Lagrange error bound to find an upper bound for $\left|f\left(2+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)-P_3\left(2+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right|$.
parts.model_answer: $|R_3(x)|\le\dfrac{48}{4!}\left|x-2\right|^4$, so at $x=2+\frac12$ the error is at most $\dfrac{48}{24}\cdot\dfrac{1}{16}=\frac{1}{8}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Lagrange error bound formula with M, the factorial 4! and the fourth power of |x - a|
Substitution of M and the distance 1/2

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Does $f$ have a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at $x=2$? Give a reason for your answer.
parts.model_answer: $f'(2)=0$ and $f''(2)=8>0$, so by the Second Derivative Test $f$ has a relative minimum at $x=2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies x = 2 as a critical point and uses the sign of f''(2)

ap_calculus_bc-f07.title: A particle with a given velocity vector: acceleration, speed, position, horizontal motion, distance

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A particle moves in the $xy$-plane so that its velocity vector at time $t\ge 0$ is $\vec v(t)=\left\langle t^2-5t,\ e^{t/2}-3\right\rangle$. At time $t=0$ the particle is at the point $(1,3)$. Find the acceleration vector of the particle at $t=1$. Is the speed of the particle increasing or decreasing at $t=1$? Give a reason for your answer.
parts.model_answer: $\vec a(t)=\langle 2t-5,\ \tfrac12e^{t/2}\rangle$, so $\vec a(1)=<-3, 0.824>$. $\vec v(1)\cdot\vec a(1)=10.886$ is positive, so the speed is increasing.

rubric_rows.criterion: Conclusion: speed is increasing, with the reason that v(1) . a(1) is positive

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the position $\bigl(x(3),y(3)\bigr)$ of the particle at time $t=3$. Write the integrals that lead to your answer.

rubric_rows.criterion: Position equals initial position plus the integral of each velocity component from 0 to 3 (setup)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For $0<t<3$, find the time at which the particle is moving horizontally (the tangent line to its path is horizontal).
parts.model_answer: The particle moves horizontally when $y'(t)=0$: $e^{t/2}=3$, so $t=2\ln 3=2.197$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets the vertical component y'(t) equal to zero (setup)

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the total distance traveled by the particle from $t=0$ to $t=3$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Integral of the speed from 0 to 3 (setup)
